text: Oliver, aged 20, purchases a ticket from AB Tickets to watch his favourite ice hockey team play in
a cup final at a stadium in London. Oliver lives a long way from London and pays in advance for
the following contracts:
• a non-refundable car hire booking with XY Rentals
• a room booking with EF Hotel.
Since making the car hire booking there has been a change in the law. All drivers must now be
aged 25 or over to hire cars. XY Rentals offers Oliver a 50% refund on the car hire.
The week before the cup final, there is a power cut at the stadium resulting in the ice melting. The
match is cancelled. AB Tickets refuses to refund Oliver’s money.
Oliver decides that he no longer needs to go to London and wants a full refund from EF Hotel.
Advise the parties as to their rights and liabilities under the doctrine of frustration. [25]
OR
Tara is employed as a law teacher at a college. Her contract requires her to teach and produce
student workbooks. The college asks Tara to produce two practice examination papers and
promises to pay her an additional £100 for this work.
Tara asks her colleague, Sandeep, to check the practice examination papers for errors. She
promises to buy him lunch for doing this work.
Martin hires Tara to work as his private tutor. Martin passes his exam with top marks and to show
his gratitude he promises to give Tara an extra £500.
Advise whether the promises made by the parties are supported by valid consideration and
therefore enforceable. [25]
Section B
Answer two questions from this section.
The aim of damages is to put claimants in the position they would have been in had the contract
been performed.
Assess the extent to which the limitations on recovery of damages provide justice for the defendant.
The rules governing intention to create legal relations in social and domestic agreements provide
justice.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
Exemption clauses are imposed upon consumers without negotiation.
Assess the extent to which the consumer is adequately protected against these clauses. [25]
